newsitem.title: ITALY: Credito sees 9-month results in line.
newsitem.headline: Credito sees 9-month results in line.

text.p: Italian banking group Credito Italiano said that its results for the first nine months of 1996 were line with its own forecasts, but it warned that 1996 had not been an easy year for the Italian banking industry.

The group's managing director and vice president, Egidio Giuseppe Bruno, made the comments while attending a news conference of the Credito/Rolo Bank grouping. Credito has a controlled stake in Rolo Bank.
He said that the results for the last part of the year were "in line with that which were forecast, but 1996 has not been an easy year for Italian banking."

Bruno also added that the bank was looking at international alliances and was currently working on an accord with a Portuguese group, but he would not give further details until the accord was completed.

The group's director general, Alessandro Profumo, added that two new companies will be formed by March next year, one to control the operating functions of the two banks and another the asset management role for the two.
